clips.text: I would keep coordination separate from technical diagnosis. I would ask the board to appoint an interim coordinator, then request another approved provider. clips.title: Reunion reflection 1: Leadership participant
clips.text: My starting point was coordination and limited continuity. The private challenge made me separate those actions from technical verification. I adapted by checking authority before access or spending and by treating the provider delay as a reason to revise instructions, not a reason to invent a recovery estimate.
clips.prompt: Explain how your approach changed.

clips.title: Reunion reflection 2: Leadership participant
clips.text: One strength was keeping coordination and technical work separate. I could improve by specifying review arrangements sooner. For the actual plan, I would propose naming an alternate coordinator, clarifying delegated authority, and testing the continuity process. Those changes would still need the appropriate organizational approval.
clips.prompt: Name one strength, one improvement, and a proposed plan change.

clips.title: Reunion reflection 1: Recovery participant

The delay challenged me to give staff useful instructions while preserving uncertainty. My final response still needed a more specific review time.
clips.prompt: Explain how your approach changed.

clips.title: Reunion reflection 2: Recovery participant
clips.text: My strength was avoiding an unsupported restoration promise. My improvement is to turn caution into a complete operational plan, with named owners and deadlines. I would ask the board to document replacement support arrangements and exercise the fallback, rather than assume an inventory entry proves recovery will work.
clips.prompt: Name one strength, one improvement, and a proposed plan change.

clips.title: Reunion reflection 1: Communications participant
